Independent CON-ASI preview probe: Wizard level 3, CON 1 -> 3 (modifier -5 -> -4), old max 6, selecting Constitution at level 4: fixed increment 0, retroactive +3, max 9; rolled natural 1 increment -3, retroactive +3, max unchanged at 6. That quote does not establish a new minimum for the level increment or maximum. The numeric clamp is correct; its state integration is not (S3).
S3. MATERIAL FINDING 1 — NEGATIVE HP PROJECTION COMMITS AN UNOWNED ZERO-HP LIFECYCLE AND CAN MAKE AN INITIALIZED CHARACTER IMMUNE TO DAMAGE. Owner: levelUpEngine projectToLiveCharacter and its HP-lifecycle integration, including initialized-zero-maximum handling. At levelUpEngine.ts:2088-2113 the new clamp sets hp_current through mutateState but never transitions life_state, conditions, death-save eligibility, or concentration. The entry guard at :541-559 only validates the OLD life state; it does not preserve the invariant after a negative delta. mutateState.ts:19-28 explicitly says this seam performs no lifecycle reactions.

Concrete reproducer at the pinned head, using real bundled resolver, in-memory SQLite, createSqliteCharacterSheetStore, valid initial alive state, XP 300 (getLevelUpEligibility returns eligible=true/currentLevel=1/targetLevel=2), immutable rollDice evidence, and Wizard level-2 choices School of Evocation plus spell:magic-missile/spell:shield:
(a) CON 6 (modifier -2), level-1 max 4/current 1, natural 1 on 1d6. applyLevelUp commits level 2, max 3/current 0/life_state alive/conditions []; sheet and progression event also commit. recordDeathSave(db,10,ctx) then throws "death saves apply only to a dying character (current state: alive)". adjustHp(db,0,ctx) throws "character lifecycle invariant I4 (0 HP character must be dying, stable, or dead) violated for 'pc-1'".
(b) CON 3 (modifier -4), level-1 max/current 2, natural 2. applyLevelUp commits level 2, max/current 0, life_state alive. adjustHp(db,-100,ctx) subsequently returns lifeState alive, instantDeath=false, deathSaveFailuresAdded=0, overflow=100; row stays alive at 0/0. hpLifecycle.ts:671-674 now mistakes a real initialized level-2 character for an uninitialized bootstrap row because hp_max===0 is its sentinel. The fixed-average CON 1/max=current=1 sibling also commits the same 0/0/alive state and survives the same damage.
(c) Control: CON 6/max=current=4/natural 1 correctly becomes max=current=3/alive; CON -1/natural 1 produces zero delta and leaves valid HP unchanged. This is the zero boundary, not all negative increments.

Authority: ADR 0020 sections 2/3 and section 5.9 conditions 6/8 retain deterministic state integrity and positively selected capability correctness. Existing runtime lifecycle contract hpLifecycle.ts:499-504 forbids alive at 0 with nonzero maximum; recordDeathSave :859-862 requires dying. Vendored rule:dropping-to-0-hit-points (records.json:151013, SRD p.97) says "When you drop to 0 hit points, you either die outright or fall unconscious"; rule:death-saving-throws (records.json:150743, p.98) says "Whenever you start your turn with 0 hit points, you must make ... a death saving throw" and, for subsequent damage at 0, "If the damage equals or exceeds your hit point maximum, you suffer instant death." Probe (b)'s 100 damage contradicts that printed rule. This finding does not assume that a nondamage level increment itself should use damage-overflow instant-death rules.

Sibling/consumer analysis: fixed, rolled and CON recompute all feed the same projectToLiveCharacter; effectiveHpMax/exhaustion clamping also feeds this current-HP write. Positive versus zero resulting maxima and positive versus zero resulting current HP were varied. The retained adjust_hp inventory at deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:300 labels the 0-max exception "(uninitialized sheet)", which no longer truthfully characterizes all reachable zero maxima. These are one lifecycle integration defect class, not separate findings. The new test levelUpEngine.test.ts:905-932 starts with seedLiveHp(db,1,0) while life_state remains alive (already invalid under I4) and only asserts two numeric columns; it cannot distinguish a coherent lifecycle from either bad state.

Required closure: integrate signed level-up HP projection with an explicitly owned, atomic lifecycle transition and distinguish initialized zero maxima from bootstrap state. Preserve attributable writes, the sourced current-HP clamp, and the source increment; do not disguise HP reduction as damage without authority or invent an automatic death rule for maximum zero. Review affected death-save/concentration/condition consumers and keep capability disclosures truthful. Permanent evidence: a generalized invariant over positive-current -> zero-current level-ups with positive and zero resulting maxima, plus a subsequent lifecycle operation/damage at initialized zero max; assert lifecycle and state ownership as well as numbers. This is proportionate because the defect changes canonical life/death and can disable all subsequent damage. Repair is MATERIAL. Required next state: repair and fresh review of the full affected HP/lifecycle boundary; PR is not approvable at this head.
S4. MATERIAL FINDING 2 — NEGATIVE MAXIMUM OUTCOMES ARE PREVIEWED AS SUPPORTED BUT THE LIVE MAXIMUM CONTRACT STILL BLOCKS ELIGIBLE SOURCE-ARITHMETIC ADVANCEMENT. Owner: levelUpEngine preview/apply and the accepted maximum-HP representation boundary. levelUpEngine.ts:835-844 and :1541-1560 correctly retain signed arithmetic, but :2080-2085 passes the resulting maximum into mutateState.ts:125, whose hp_max descriptor requires an integer >=0. The Captain's clamp at :2097 affects hp_current only and is reached after the hp_max write.

Concrete independent reproducer at 032e90a3: initialized alive Wizard level 1, CON 3/modifier -4, maximum/current 2 (6-4, the actual level-1 formula), XP 300. getLevelUpEligibility returns eligible=true, pendingLevels=1. Supply the real level-2 required choices and rollDice('1d6',{nextInt:()=>0}) (natural 1). previewLevelUpChangeSet returns ok=true, increment=-3, maximum {from:2,to:-1}. applyLevelUp then throws "MutateStateError: character.hp_max must be an integer >= 0". SQLite sheet, live level/HP and event ledger all roll back: sheet/live level 1, max/current 2, zero progression events. Atomic rollback is correct; rejection of this otherwise supported eligible advancement and the preview/apply boundary are unresolved. The failure is not caused by malformed dice, missing choices, ineligibility, dying state, or multiclassing. The same writer receives fixed-average and CON-recomputed negative maxima; creation does not contain a substitute per-level floor.

Authority: owning bead .19.6.7.9 acceptance requires exact roll/fixed value + CON with no invented floor and handling nonpositive increments; its design specifically requires inspecting downstream validation and reporting a lower-bound conflict rather than inventing a source rule. The review assignment explicitly includes negative hp_max outcomes and legitimate level-ups. SRD p.56 rule:beyond-1st-level (records.json:148832) says "add the total to your hit point maximum"; p.81 rule:constitution-hit-points (records.json:150044) retains retroactive arithmetic. Neither supplies a per-level floor or an alternative outcome at this boundary. ADR 0020 sections 2/3 and section 5.9 condition 6 require explicit operation/input/exclusion semantics and correct retained capabilities. level-up-v1 at deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:1934-1953 claims one-step application with fixed/rolled HP and has no declared negative-maximum boundary. The implementer report checked signed gains, but the existing hp_max>=0 downstream constraint was not resolved by the report or Captain's current-HP clamp.

This finding DOES NOT assert that the printed source explicitly defines a negative live-maximum lifecycle, nor authorize blindly permitting negative hp_max throughout the engine. The demonstrated defect is the unresolved source-arithmetic/live-representation boundary and rejection of a supported eligible input. Required closure: explicitly reconcile maximum-HP representation and adjudication/state ownership under the governing authority so preview and apply agree and legitimate source-specified advancement has a coherent atomic outcome. If a bounded exclusion or adjudication is required, obtain that authority and disclose it truthfully; do not silently restore a per-level floor, clamp the calculated maximum by invention, or weaken tests to match refusal. Permanent evidence: a generalized integration invariant spanning positive, zero and negative computed maxima from valid initialized/eligible states, comparing preview, canonical sheet, live state and ledger/rollback. A small table at this boundary is proportionate; multiple near-identical exact reproducers are unnecessary. Repair is MATERIAL. Required next state: resolve this boundary in the current repair and re-review, rather than closing A2-F4 on arithmetic alone.
